long_biography.plain_text:
Industrial expansion in Africa became a defining chapter of Sri Prakash Lohia's work. After his group bought Nigeria's Eleme Petrochemicals in 2006, he oversaw its return to profit and personally travelled to the country when two employees were kidnapped the following year. The acquisition extended an enterprise begun in Indonesia with M.L. Lohia decades earlier.

Today he chairs the Singapore-based parent, while Amit Lohia helps direct operations as group vice-chairman. A trust benefiting their immediate family controls the Indonesian listed subsidiary. Aloke Lohia's Thailand-listed Indorama Ventures is an associated but separately managed concern, although Sri Prakash holds an investment and a non-executive board role there. Beyond manufacturing, he has opened his extensive hand-coloured rare-book collection to the public through a free digital archive.
